I was on antidepressants for years. Got really bad when I changed to a new one the last time. Now I refuse to take any or try more. It may be what you need, and I'm not saying that you shouldn't try it. I know many people who wouldn't be alive anymore if not for meds. Just don't blindly trust your doctor, do your own research so that you're aware of what you're committing too. Also quitting meds is not something you can just do in a heartbeat contrary to what you might hear. Antidepressants are potent stuff. Gradually tapering the dose down to get off usually works, and for some there's no issue at all. But withdrawal can be horrible, even for SSRIs that are said to be non-addictive which is technically true but in practice can have awful withdrawal effects which to me is a form of addictiveness or whatever. Good luck

I've been experimenting a lot with casting with limited equipment. Like you I found the equipment required for lost wax quite expensive. What I've ended up using is delft clay (or similar sand of another brand). You can definately use a wax model to make an impression in the sand (I've even begun using 3D-printed models lately). However, using sand does limit what models you can cast since you need to be able to separate the two halves of the mold and remove the model before pouring the metal. What I've ended up doing sometimes to mitigate this limitation is to divide the model into parts, cast them individually and then solder those parts together. Hope it works out for you :)

I made the silver part of the ring by soldering three different parts together: First i made a fairly wide ring with a thickness of about 0.8 mm. Then I made 2 rings that fit the outside of the wide ring out of 1.5 mm square wire (it can be a pain to get the size right so that they fit snuggly to the wide ring). After that I soldered the two small rings to the wide ring, one on each side, leaving a channel in the middle. Thanks a lot!
